title: Network Analysis of Deceptive Information Spread: Can AI Deception Be Modeled as a Contagion?
original_idea: Model a simplified information ecosystem of LLM-using agents sharing outputs. Inject a single deceptively-aligned model. Simulate information spread using epidemiological contagion models (SIR). Measure propagation dynamics and identify structural mitigations.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: deceptive AI outputs spread through information networks -> contagion modeling identifies structural mitigations. Names a specific mechanism but the gap is whether SIR models meaningfully apply to information ecosystems with LLM agents -- the analogy may be too loose to produce actionable insights.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: SIR modeling and network simulation are well-established with available libraries (NetworkX, etc.). However, designing a meaningful information ecosystem simulation with LLM agents requires both network science and multi-agent system knowledge. The simulation design is the challenging part.

narrow_scope.reasoning: A first deliverable exists (SIR simulation on a simple network with one deceptive source), but the simulation requires multiple design decisions (network structure, information sharing rules, what constitutes 'infection'). Moderate effort to first result.

novelty.reasoning: SIR-based models for misinformation spread are well-established, including recent work with AI-generated content ('Modeling the dynamics of misinformation spread' Frontiers 2025, with GIFS model incorporating generative AI). Multi-agent information co-evolution models on various network topologies (ER, BA, WS) have been validated against traditional SIR models. Secret collusion among AI agents via steganography has been studied (NeurIPS 2024). The specific framing of a 'deceptively-aligned model' as a contagion source is somewhat novel, but the underlying epidemiological modeling methodology for AI-generated misinformation is well-covered. The gap is narrow: existing models study misinformation spread generally, not specifically deceptive alignment contagion in LLM-agent ecosystems.
